summary: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Gyume Tantric College and Sera Monastery, earning his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and later taught Artemus Bertine Engle.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Losang Chödar served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics and held a post at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, both attested in 2010.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Leiden University in 1960 and Drepung Monastery, where he served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Palden Drakpa was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, where his affiliation is attested from 1987 to 2004.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933–2013) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After studying at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as a teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from circa 1978 to 2013.

Geshe Tashi Tsering works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Lharampa Geshe at Sera Monastery, studied at Gyuto Monastery under Geshe Thubten Rinchen, and held teaching posts at Kopan Monastery, Gandhi Foundation College, and Jamyang Buddhist Centre.
Geshe Tsondru Namgyal is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned Geshe degrees studying at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery, and he taught Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.

Geshe Wangyal (1901–1983) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Agvan Dorjiev and at Drepung Monastery (~1923–1938). He later taught at Columbia University (~1967–1976) and at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983), which he founded.
Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held a post as a scholar at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested between 1991 and 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden (1926–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche, later teaching at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1969).
Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University from circa 1895 to 1898 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1901 until 1926.

Giacomella Orofino specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" circa 1992.
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda (1888–1953) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, where he later served as professeur adjoint from 1934 to 1948, and also held a post at Rissho University.

Gikyo Ito (1909–1996) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1949–1968) and Kyoto Sangyo University (~1968–1980).

Gil Fronsdal works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, among others, and held posts at the Insight Meditation Center (~1992) and Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997).

Gilles Tarabout specializes in Indology and religious studies. In 2004, he was attested holding posts at CNRS as a senior fellow, EHESS as a member, and FMSH as director of the Indo-French exchange program in social sciences.

Gin Ling Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Liu earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun, both attested in 2008.

Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) was a philosopher who studied at Scuola Normale Superiore and University of Florence. He held posts at Palermo, Pisa, Sapienza University of Rome, Bocconi, and Scuola Normale Superiore, and was president of IsMEO in 1933.

Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Genoa (~1891–1897) and subsequently held academic posts at the University of Florence (~1911–1922) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1923–1947).
